title: Work IQ: policy-based governance of agents and their capabilities
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, navigation paths and automation calls are supported, and it distinguishes existing MCP controls from the planned change. The description of the policy layer as a single switch needs narrowing, and differing Microsoft guidance on default write access should be acknowledged.

claims.quote: Provide administrators with policy-based controls for governing agents and their capabilities at scale.

claims.claim: Work IQ uses a Rego-based policy layer.
claims.quote: The policy layer uses Rego, the policy language from Open Policy Agent (OPA), to express authorization rules.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy evaluates tool requests at request time, including requests from existing callers.
claims.quote: When you turn on the policy, it applies across the tenant and helps control MCP tool access at request time.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Policy can restrict the resource paths used by Work IQ MCP requests.
claims.quote: For example, a tenant policy can allow read access to common productivity data while blocking high-risk paths, write operations, or large collection traversal.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Policy can restrict the operations and capabilities used by Work IQ MCP requests.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy can govern data retrieval limits.
claims.quote: Data retrieval limits | Whether collection reads are bounded to reduce large-scale data extraction risk

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Initial-release Work IQ MCP policy can be turned on or off tenant-wide in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Per-user, per-app, per-agent and scenario-specific policy templates are outside the initial Work IQ MCP policy control surface.
claims.quote: Per-user, per-app, per-agent, or scenario-specific policy templates aren't part of the initial policy control surface.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Mutation operations, including create, update, delete and actions such as sending email, are disallowed by default.
claims.quote: By default, mutation operations aren't allowed for safety. This restriction includes create, update, delete, and action requests that modify data, such as sending email.
claims.fix: Keep this attributed to the MCP policy guide, but add: 'The Copilot Studio Work IQ guide separately says write operations are on by default, subject to organisational permissions and policies; check the applicable experience rather than assuming a uniform write default.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/add-work-iq#work-iq-key-features, which states 'Write operations are on by default. Your organization's permissions and policies still apply.'

claims.claim: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy.
claims.quote: Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing Microsoft 365 permissions.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ API use is metered through consumption of Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: You pay for use of the Work IQ API through a consumption-based model that uses Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Spending policies can include or exclude Work IQ API.
claims.quote: Include Cowork and exclude Work IQ API from a policy when its users shouldn't consume credits through Work IQ API.

claims.claim: Spending policies can set spending limits for covered services and users.
claims.quote: Set policy and per-user limits | Limit monthly consumption for selected user groups and the services covered by their policies.

claims.claim: Spending policies do not reserve credits for a workload, user or group.
claims.quote: Spending policies control access and spending limits; they don't reserve or allocate credits for a workload, user, or group.

claims.claim: The tenant policy UI is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.

claims.claim: No automation call for the Work IQ MCP tenant policy switch is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" "policy" "graph" "beta"; "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "API" "settings" "endpoint". Read policy governance page and search excerpts covering Graph beta and Work IQ references; no endpoint or command for changing this switch was found.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP server access can be blocked at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools. ... Select Work IQ MCP. ... To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent to the Work IQ MCP server Block control is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP server block access Microsoft Graph beta API tool management; "Work IQ MCP" "block" "site:learn.microsoft.com/graph". Read access-control guide and search results; commands found for other MCP servers did not establish this control's API.

claims.claim: No native admin-center setting is documented for provisioning the Work IQ API service principal.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ API enable tenant service principal admin center UI Graph Explorer. Read Enable your tenant for Work IQ and Foundry setup excerpts; the tab labelled Admin center directs readers to a Graph Explorer POST, not an admin-center configuration path.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals with appId fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 provisions the Work IQ service principal.
claims.quote: Set the method to POST and the URL to https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals. ... { "appId": "fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7" }

claims.claim: The Work IQ service principal can alternatively be provisioned with az ad sp create --id <appId>.
claims.quote: Create the Work IQ service principal in your organization by running the following command. ... az ad sp create --id fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7

claims.claim: Grant consent is at Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > App registrations > app > API permissions > Grant admin consent for [your tenant].
claims.quote: Grant consent: In the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Entra ID > App registrations > select the app > API permissions. Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant].

claims.claim: Revoke consent is on the app's API permissions page by selecting WorkIQAgent.Ask and Revoke admin consent.
claims.quote: Revoke consent: On the same API permissions page, select the WorkIQAgent.Ask permission and select Revoke admin consent.

claims.where: controls[3].api; Governance controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: az ad app permission admin-consent --id <appId> grants admin consent for the registered application.
claims.quote: Add the WorkIQAgent.Ask delegated permission and grant consent. ... az ad app permission admin-consent --id $APP_ID

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: For the documented consent procedure, the application must first request WorkIQAgent.Ask.
claims.quote: Select API permissions, Add a permission, and then APIs my organization uses. Search for Work IQ, and then select Delegated permissions. Select WorkIQAgent.Ask and then select Add permissions.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Governance controls table; Governance controls
claims.claim: The quickstart uses az ad app permission add to request the delegated permission before running admin-consent.
claims.quote:
az ad app permission add --id $APP_ID \
  --api fdcc1f02-fc51-4226-8753-f668596af7f7 \
  --api-permissions "0b1715fd-f4bf-4c63-b16d-5be31f9847c2=Scope"
az ad app permission admin-consent --id $APP_ID

claims.claim: In the initial release the policy layer is a single tenant-level switch.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ MCP" "policy" "API" "settings" "endpoint". Read Policy governance for Work IQ MCP in full: it documents a tenant on/off control, supported mutation configuration and toggle-style and numeric settings, but does not reduce the layer to one switch.
claims.fix: Replace 'In the initial release the policy layer is a single tenant-level switch' with 'In the initial release, Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level'. Keep the subsequent statement about templates, supported by https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/work-iq/mcp/policy-governance-mcp.

claims.claim: More granular policy controls and templates are described as possible later additions, not committed capabilities.
claims.quote: More granular controls and policy templates might be added later based on customer requests, feedback, and usage.
